propositions: Pandoc 3.6.1 escapes punctuation inside code spans, deletes HTML comments, and corrupts arrow delimiters, requiring a post-render code-preservation check where every source code fragment must appear verbatim in output or the unit falls back to original Markdown.

A two-phase left-to-right lexer locks protected blocks (noformat spans, HTML comments, backtick/tilde fences, four-space indents) before segmentation, then classifies unlocked content through six ordered rules (safe passthrough, Jira markers, ASCII tables, HTML tags, regex-dangerous prose, pandoc rendering).

An inline-Jira scanner must distinguish unambiguous wiki markers ({{monospace}}, [label|target], {color:name}) that settle a unit alone from ambiguous CommonMark markers (*strong*, _emphasis_) that only settle units with no CommonMark-only syntax, preventing re-rendering cycles.

A deterministic corpus of 178 bodies (29 code-arrow, 29 table, 120 prose) with pinned counts and fixed seed measures rendering fidelity at body ratio >=0.90 and character ratio >=0.95, ensuring non-silent store corruption.

The wiki extra pins pypandoc-binary==1.15 bundling pandoc 3.6.1, registers as optional dependency with joint-extra CI, and provides content-free fallback logging with reasons pandoc_absent, conversion_failure, or preservation_failure.
WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound, OutboundFieldMapper, live sends, and all existing wiki codec methods remain unchanged; the unwired renderer is isolated and requires Story 3388 for cutover.
